A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPEFT study and have readable text, equations, figures, and tables across all 14 pages. The appendices are complete: A-B in v1 and A-D in v2. Retained content can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning results on GLUE, MMLU, and GSM8K, together with experiments comparing salience metrics and masking strategies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Llama3-8b code-generation evaluations and a parameter-budget sensitivity study.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same sparse adaptation procedure, eight salience metrics, global/local selection, and static/dynamic mask updates. The additional experiments apply the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds training on CodeFeedback and evaluation on HumanEval and MBPP, extending coverage to executable code generation. The earlier GLUE, conversational fine-tuning/MMLU, and MetaMathQA/GSM8K coverage remains.

E2.justification: Figure 2 adds PiSSA to the Gemma2-2b/GSM8K comparison through the new budget sweep. v1 evaluated PiSSA on GLUE, but its GSM8K comparison included LoRA and a pretrained reference without PiSSA. Comparator membership in the retained result tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a controlled budget sweep with LoRA ranks from 4 to 128, alpha equal to rank, and matched sparse parameter counts. Code evaluations introduce Llama3-8b and Pass@1 metrics. Separately, Section 4 and Table 3 change the reported GSM8K setting from 8-shot to 5-shot while retaining every score; the PDFs do not establish whether this corrects documentation or reflects rerunning.

E4.justification: New Appendix C and Figure 2 investigate parameter efficiency across six trainable-parameter budgets using flexible-extract and strict-match scores. This adds a substantive sensitivity analysis of the efficiency-performance trade-off. The original static/dynamic and global/local masking ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs and standard deviations for the same smaller GLUE models, including the same uncertainty statement in Table 4. The new code results and budget plots add no run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds code-generation scores in Table 12 and budget-dependent results in Figure 2. Table 12 reports averages of 49.39 for Gradient, 44.83 for LoRA, and 49.40 for Taylor-FO. All numerical entries in the original main result tables and corresponding GLUE appendix tables are retained, including GSM8K scores despite the changed shot description.

T1.justification: The optimization objective, sparsity constraints, salience formulas, and global/local mask definitions in Section 3 are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new empirical budget analysis introduces no formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a systematic eight-metric evaluation, strong gradient-based static SPEFT, and little benefit from dynamic masking. The new experiments support these retained claims. The abstract's description of the existing open-source resource as a reproducible benchmark does not materially redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C interprets the new sweep as showing that gradient-based SPEFT can outperform LoRA with fewer trainable parameters and widen its advantage as budgets increase. It also discusses comparable FLOPs under matched budgets. The existing hardware discussion, salience interpretation, and limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Table 8 documents CodeFeedback training settings, including AdamW, one epoch, batch size 16, learning rate 2E-5, sequence length 512, and adapter budgets. Appendix C specifies the rank/alpha sweep. Existing hyperparameters, code-access information, hardware, and runtime disclosures are retained; computational resources move to Appendix D.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting HumanEval, MBPP, Llama 3, CodeFeedback, and MRPC. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to LoRA, sparse adaptation, and pruning proxies remain substantially unchanged. Citation-style changes and the expanded Gemma reference are bibliographic presentation updates.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 makes localized wording corrections, completes the generation-experiment description, adds acknowledgments, and moves computational resources into the appendix. The new scientific material does not entail extensive rewriting of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint layout to two columns, extensively resizing and relocating tables, captions, and text. Figure 2 and Tables 8 and 12 are new displays. Figure 1 and the original tables are retained, with appendix tables reordered and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The code-generation evaluations and controlled budget sweep strengthen empirical support for task generality and parameter efficiency. These are useful, limited gains. Reporting issues temper them: Table 12 gives FORCE an average of 34.91 despite component scores of 46.95 and 50.4, and unchanged GSM8K scores are relabeled from 8-shot to 5-shot without explanation. The revision improves coverage and analysis without resolving broader evidential limitations.
